Hi Priya / Alex,

Thanks again for the quick call today — good alignment on pilot goals. Below is a concise recap and the specific asks we need to finalize sizing and an SLO matrix for the pilot. Please confirm or correct the bolded numbers by end of day Tuesday so we can lock capacity and pricing: 

High-level objectives
- Pilot (~8 weeks) to validate extraction and semantic search for clinical notes ingestion.
- Tight latency for UX: 95th percentile generation latency target 300ms for standard prompts; streaming for longer sessions.

What we heard / items to confirm (please reply inline):
1) Steady-state traffic (expected): ~25 QPS (non-streaming) across the day — average request ~300 tokens.
2) Peak crest behavior: **~220 QPS** for short bursts (30–120s) during batch ingests / ETL spikes — occurs ~4–6x/day.
3) Streaming: up to **60 concurrent** streaming sessions (avg. 3–5 min), each producing ~20 tokens/sec on average.
4) SLA targets: 95th perc. steady requests <300ms, max tail allowance to 700ms during peaks; streaming initial chunk <200ms.
5) Data residency: US only; logs retained 30 days.

Attachments: hydra_sample_traffic.csv (sample 1-hour trace, anonymized) — attached to this thread.

Next steps we propose
- Please confirm numbers above or paste corrected values.
- If correct, Karthik will produce a first-pass capacity plan (tokens/sec, recommended GPU pool, autoscale knobs) and Marissa will draft the pilot SLO doc + canary rollout plan.
- We’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up to review the sizing doc.

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming / clarifying the numbers from our side: 

- Steady-state: 22–28 QPS (we'll use 25 QPS as the working number). Average payload ~300 tokens/request (range 120–900).
- Peak crest: we see up to 210–240 QPS during ETL bursts; typical crest duration ~60–90s, happens roughly 4x/day, sometimes 6x if multiple pipelines align.
- Streaming: expect spikes up to 55–65 concurrent streams during the crest window; average streaming session length ~4 minutes; token emission from model averages 15–25 tokens/sec depending on prompt.
- Concurrency for non-streaming long jobs: occasionally 140 concurrent short sync requests for backfill windows.
- SLA: target 95p generation latency ~300ms is OK; we can tolerate up to 800ms in peak crest for a small percentage of requests.

Jordan / Marissa — first-pass sizing notes below. High-level assumptions: 300 tokens/request avg, 25 QPS steady, crest 230 QPS for 90s, streaming concurrency up to 60 during crest. Model pick: rw-13b-quant (fp16/Q4) for pilot to balance latency and cost.

1) Tokens/sec math
- Steady: 25 QPS * 300 tokens = 7,500 tokens/sec
- Crest (sustained for planning): 230 QPS * 300 tokens = 69,000 tokens/sec
- Worst-case 95th tokens/request: assume 700 tokens => 230 * 700 = 161,000 tokens/sec (safety envelope)

2) GPU pool recommendation (NVIDIA A100-style perf proxy)
- Baseline pool: 4 GPUs (shared, steady handling + autoscale headroom)
- Autoscale to 10 GPUs during crest (policy: scale when 95p queue latency > 200ms or tokens/sec > 60k)
- Rationale: rw-13b-quant can serve ~7.5k tokens/sec per GPU at target tail latency ~300ms in our test harness for non-streaming short prompts; for streaming, CPU/GPU pinning reduces throughput per GPU, so we reserve 1 GPU capacity equivalent per ~8 concurrent streams.

3) Streaming memory footprint (rough)
- KV cache + per-session state: ~300–600 MB per concurrent stream depending on prompt length and model variant (13B quant tends low-end); plan 0.6 GB/stream as conservative.
- For 60 concurrent streams: ~36 GB GPU memory reserved (or pinned across nodes), which maps to ~1–2 GPUs depending on instance memory. We'll model streaming placement to avoid OOMs and keep steady-gen GPUs separate from streaming workers if needed.

4) Canary & fallback plan
- Canary: Kick off with 10% traffic on a single GPU pool with rw-13b-quant, validate tail latencies & memory under streaming conditions for 48h.
- Fallback: If crest tail > 800ms or OOMs, fallback to smaller context reduces (truncate last N tokens) and route to a cheaper variant rw-6b-quant for non-critical requests.

5) Open questions for external
- Confirm maximum acceptable crest duration and how often double-crest can occur (concurrent crest windows).
- Confirm tolerance for staging streaming sessions on separate GPU nodes (i.e., not co-located with gen pool).

I'll put these notes into a short sizing doc and share a link. If this aligns, we can provision a test pool and schedule the Thur 9am PT review.

-Karthik
